text: Because Missus Mallard was afflicted. <break time="0.8s" /> With heart trouble. <break time="0.8s" /> Great care was taken. <break time="0.8s" /> To break the news. <break time="0.8s" /> Of her husbands death. <break time="0.8s" /> To her. <break time="0.8s" /> As gently as possible. <break time="0.8s" /> It was her sister Josephine. <break time="0.8s" /> Who told her. <break time="0.8s" /> In broken sentences. <break time="0.8s" /> And veiled hints. <break time="0.8s" /> That revealed the truth. <break time="0.8s" /> While half hiding it. <break time="0.8s" /> Her husbands friend Richards. <break time="0.8s" /> Was there too. <break time="0.8s" /> Because he had been in the newspaper office. <break time="0.8s" /> When news of the railroad disaster arrived. <break time="0.8s" /> Brently Mallards name. <break time="0.8s" /> Had led the list of the killed. <break time="0.8s" /> And Richards. <break time="0.8s" /> Who wanted to be sure. <break time="0.8s" /> Had checked it. <break time="0.8s" /> With a second telegram. <break time="0.8s" /> He had then hurried. <break time="0.8s" /> To the Mallards house. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping to arrive. <break time="0.8s" /> Before any less careful and less tender friend. <break time="0.8s" /> Could bring the sad message. <break time="0.8s" /> She did not hear the story. <break time="0.8s" /> As many women have heard the same. <break time="0.8s" /> With a frozen inability to accept. <break time="0.8s" /> What it meant. <break time="0.8s" /> She wept at once. <break time="0.8s" /> With sudden, wild abandonment. <break time="0.8s" /> In her sisters arms. <break time="0.8s" /> And her whole body shook. <break time="0.8s" /> With the force of her tears. <break time="0.8s" /> When the storm of grief. <break time="0.8s" /> Had spent itself. <break time="0.8s" /> She went away to her room alone. <break time="0.8s" /> And she would have no one follow her.
